title: Scientific Calculator
description: A full scientific calculator with trigonometry, logarithms, powers, and roots, right in your browser.

formula.summary: Expressions are parsed with a hand-written tokenizer and recursive-descent parser (not JavaScript's eval) and evaluated left-to-right respecting standard operator precedence.
formula.expression: + − × ÷ ^ % with sin, cos, tan, log, ln, sqrt, and parentheses

faqs.question: Are angles in degrees or radians?
faqs.answer: Trigonometric functions use radians, matching standard mathematical and programming convention. To use degrees, multiply by pi/180 first, e.g. sin(45 * pi/180).

faqs.question: What functions are supported?
faqs.answer: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, log (base 10), ln (natural log), sqrt, cbrt, abs, exp, round, floor, ceil, plus +, −, ×, ÷, ^ (power), % (modulo), and factorial (!).

faqs.question: Is it safe to paste in arbitrary text?
faqs.answer: Yes - the calculator never executes JavaScript from your input. It uses a custom parser that only understands numbers, operators, and the specific function names listed above, and rejects anything else with an error.

seoContent.heading: A real scientific calculator, safely evaluated
seoContent.body: Many online 'calculators' evaluate your input with JavaScript's eval() or new Function(), which can be a security risk. This one uses a dedicated tokenizer and recursive-descent parser built specifically for arithmetic, so it only ever understands numbers, operators, and a fixed set of named functions - never arbitrary code.

seoContent.heading: Operator precedence and functions
seoContent.body: The parser respects standard order of operations: parentheses first, then exponentiation, then multiplication/division/modulo, then addition/subtraction, with unary minus and factorial handled at the appropriate precedence level - the same rules taught in school and used by graphing calculators.
